ssv-network.upside: SSV runs Ethereum's largest distributed-validator network and has real staking use; a DAO partner-program vote around Nov 29 is the only dated item, and it is minor.
ssv-network.cheap: It isn't ignored now: up 76% in a week, and SSV Labs proposed cutting new development in October, which explains much of the long slide.
ssv-network.wrongIf: The weekly gain fully reverses (back under about $1.60) or the development-cut proposal passes with no new product plan.
ssv-network.vsScanner: The scanner's TokoCrypto 'new listing' could not be confirmed, and a 76% week on 4x volume is a spike, not an entry.

tagger.upside: An AI data-labeling business that says it settles B2B deals in USD1 and buys back TAG with revenue; nothing dated is coming.
tagger.cheap: Only 27% of tokens are released and a large treasury could sell, so the market discounts it for supply.
tagger.wrongIf: Trading falls back under $5M a day or the price gives back this week's 42% gain.
tagger.vsScanner: A 20x volume spike with no news I could find; the score jump is momentum, not a story.

mori-finance-2.upside: A small working covered-call options product on Solana, fresh out of its MetaDAO sale; a first centralized exchange listing would be the event, but none is announced.
mori-finance-2.cheap: It isn't cheap: it trades near 3.9x its $0.025 sale price and close to its Nov 14 high, on one DEX pool.
mori-finance-2.wrongIf: Price falls back under $0.05, or options volume does not grow past October's level.
mori-finance-2.vsScanner: Scanner sees a +59% week; I see a freshly sold token already far above its sale price with about $120K a day of trading.

zano.upside: Active privacy chain with a roadmap (mobile wallet and execution layer in Q4 2026, pure proof-of-stake 'Zenith' in Q2 2027), but the dates are soft.
zano.cheap: In October a bug let an attacker mint about 36.9M ZANO and the chain was rolled back a month, which hurts trust; privacy coins also face exchange pressure.
zano.wrongIf: Any further exploit or rollback, or the Q4 2026 wallet and execution-layer releases slip into 2027.
zano.vsScanner: The new listings (XT.COM, Hotcoin, Nonkyc) are tiny venues; the scanner has no flag for the October exploit and rollback, which is the bigger fact.

netx.upside: Small payments/RWA chain; still no dated upgrade or listing found.
netx.cheap: Barely known, two exchanges; no clear reason it is mispriced.
netx.wrongIf: No dated upgrade or new listing by end of December, or price falls back under $0.12 (my first-pick level).
netx.vsScanner: Up 35% in a day with no news found; my 11-17 'wrong if' has not triggered, but nothing new supports it either.

logicnet.upside: Subnet 35 (Cartha) powers liquidity for 0xMarkets, whose trading front end is still on testnet; a mainnet launch is the event.
logicnet.cheap: Not cheap: about 7.5x since first picked, in a $390K token with $73K a day of trading.
logicnet.wrongIf: The 0xMarkets exchange is not live on mainnet by end of December 2026.
logicnet.vsScanner: Another +30% day with no new announcement; still a blown-out spike.

topPicksNote: No coin has a verified, dated catalyst: the strongest names (SSV, Tagger, Mori) already jumped 40-76% this week on unexplained volume, and the rest are zombies, delisted, exploited or not real coins.

sectorNews.DeFi: DeFi locked value is down about 39% this year to roughly $70B, and mid-November brought another lending exploit (Kava Lend, about $3.8M) and outflows from Spark. That backdrop hurts small DeFi tokens; money is not rotating into them.
sectorNews.AI: I found no clearly dated AI-sector story for the past week; recent recaps describe choppy, mixed weeks with small AI tokens hit hardest in sell-offs. No sector wave is lifting small AI names right now.
sectorNews.RWA: Tokenized real-world assets keep growing (about $40B on chain by Nov 18, led by Ondo and Securitize), but the growth goes to large issuers and tokenized funds, not to small RWA tokens like Credefi or Mintlayer.
sectorNews.Governance: No sector-specific news; governance tokens move with their underlying projects. Both of today's names (Alchemix, Cookie DAO) are near all-time lows with no governance catalyst.
